insight.title: Why Being Slightly Inconvenient Makes You More Desirable
insight.subtitle: How adding a small hurdle increases the perceived value of your work

sections.text: High-end restaurants often hide their phone numbers, and luxury brands rarely list prices upfront. While we strive for frictionless business, total ease often signals that what you offer is common and low-value.

Try this today: When you remove every barrier, you remove the psychological reward of earning access. Strategic friction filters out the wrong audience and forces high-value partners to acknowledge that your time is a premium resource.

Most people think being hyper-available wins clients, but it actually creates a commodity mindset. Strategy is about choosing where to add hurdles, ensuring that only those who truly value your work reach you.
When you receive a request today, ask for a brief written summary before agreeing to meet.
Value is rarely found in the path of least resistance.

news.title: IMF Chief Warns of Economic Impact on Global Growth Due to Middle East Conflict
news.description: IMF Chief Kristalina Georgieva anticipates increased demand for IMF financial support owing to global economic challenges arising from the Middle East conflict. The war's impact, including significant cuts in oil and gas supplies, disrupts global growth forecasts, increases food insecurity, and influences inflation. A unified international response is urged.
news.why: A global economic slowdown reduces your chances of getting a salary raise.

news.title: IMF expects to provide vulnerable economies hit by Iran war up to $50 bn
news.description: The International Monetary Fund expects to have to provide up to $50 billion in immediate financial assistance to countries affected by the Middle East war, its managing director said on Thursday, with the crisis likely to have lasting economic effects."Given the spillovers of the Middle East war, we expect near-term demand for IMF balance-of-payments support to rise to somewhere between $20 billion and $50 billion, with the lower bound prevailing if the ceasefire holds," Kristalina Georgieva said, according to prepared remarks shared with AFP.
news.why: This support prevents local banks from closing during the conflict.

news.title: Lebanon's Hospitals Face Critical Shortage Amid Escalating Conflict
news.description: Lebanon's hospitals are on the brink of running out of essential trauma kits due to recent Israeli strikes. The World Health Organization warns that the shortage could lead to dire consequences for treating war-related injuries. Supplies dwindled after mass casualties, further strained by Gulf war disruptions.
news.why: Regional strikes are cutting off access to life-saving trauma kits in hospitals.
